mechanism_narrative: A 2% quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strengthening economic demand, leading to increased consumer spending and, subsequently, higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of quarters with 2%+ GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.5%, signaling a tightening monetary cycle, S&P 500 forward returns tend to decline over the next 20 trading days due to increased borrowing costs.
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns remain positive in > 70% of periods with FEDFUNDS above 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Jointly, when UNRATE falls below 6% and PAYEMS growth exceeds 200,000 over 3 months, the strengthening labor market indicates increased consumer power, driving S&P 500 returns higher over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward SPX returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A 5% monthly increase in INDPRO signals increased industrial production, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic growth.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) exceeds 1,200,000 units, indicating strong demand for housing, S&P 500 returns tend to increase over the next 60 trading days due to the positive impact on related sectors.
failure_condition: 60-day forward SPX returns are negative in > 45% of periods with HOUST above 1,200,000 units.

mechanism_narrative: Always, the level of FEDFUNDS inversely correlates with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as higher rates increase borrowing costs across the economy.
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns do not inversely correlate with FEDFUNDS levels in > 55% of observations.

mechanism_narrative: If UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% in one month, signaling labor market stress, and PAYEMS growth is negative over the same period, S&P 500 returns tend to decline over the next 5 trading days due to decreased consumer confidence.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increase > 0.5% and PAYEMS < 0 over 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward SPX returns are positive in > 50% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) grows by more than 8% annually, indicating strong consumer demand, S&P 500 returns tend to increase over the next 60 trading days, reflecting the positive economic outlook.
failure_condition: 60-day forward SPX returns are negative in > 40% of periods with RSAFS annual growth above 8%.
